<td style="width:6%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left">3.9</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; text-align: left; line-height: normal;"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Non-current assets held for sale</div> </div> </td> </tr> </table> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Bank reclassifies in this category non-current assets of which the carrying amount will be recovered principally through a sale transaction rather than through continuing use. The asset (or disposal group) must be available for immediate sale in its present condition subject only to terms that are usual and customary for sales of such assets (or disposal groups) and its sale must be highly probable. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Non-current assets classified as held for sale are measured, when they are reclassified to this category, at the lower of carrying amount and fair value less costs to sell and are disclosed in a separate item in the consolidated statement of financial position. Once these assets are classified as held for sale, depreciation and amortization ceased. </div> <div style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 13%;text-indent: 0px;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Profit or loss generated in the sale of assets held for sale is recorded in the consolidated statement of income as &#8220;Other operating income&#8221;. </div></div></div> </ix:nonNumeric> <div style="font-size: 6pt; margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px;">&#160;</div> <ix:nonNumeric name="ifrs-full:DescriptionOfAccountingPolicyForImpairmentOfNonfinancialAssetsExplanatory" contextRef="P01_01_2024To12_31_2024" escape="true" id="ixv-58167">

<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; text-align: left; line-height: normal;"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Impairment of non-financial assets</div> </div> </td> </tr> </table> <div style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 13%;text-indent: 0px;"><div style="display:inline;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">The Bank evaluates, at least at each fiscal year-end, whether there are any events or changes in the circumstances that may indicate the impairment of non-financial assets or whether there is any evidence that a non-financial asset may be impaired. </div></div></div> <div style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 13%;text-indent: 0px;"><div style="display:inline;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">When there is any evidence or when an annual impairment test is required for an asset, the Bank shall estimate the recoverable amount of such asset. As of the date of issuance of these consolidated Financial Statements, there is no evidence of impairment of non-financial assets and the recoverable amount are higher than the related carrying amount. </div></div></div> </ix:nonNumeric> <div style="font-size: 6pt; margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px;">&#160;</div> <ix:nonNumeric name="ifrs-full:DescriptionOfAccountingPolicyForProvisionsExplanatory" contextRef="P01_01_2024To12_31_2024" escape="true" id="ixv-58182">

<td style="width:6%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left">3.11</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; text-align: left; line-height: normal;"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Provisions</div> </div> </td> </tr> </table> <div style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 13%;text-indent: 0px;"><div style="display:inline;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">The Bank recognizes a provision if and only if the following circumstances are met: (a)&#160;the Bank has a present obligation as a result of a past event; (b)&#160;it is probable (i.e. it is more likely than not) that an outflow of resources embodying economic benefits will be required to settle the obligation; and (c)&#160;a reliable estimate can be made of the amount of the obligation. </div></div></div> <div style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 13%;text-indent: 0px;"><div style="display:inline;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">In order to determine the amount of provisions, the risks and uncertainties were considered taking into account the opinion of independent and internal legal advisors of the Bank. Where the effect of the time value of money is material, the provisions shall be discounted using a pre-tax rate that reflects, if applicable, current risks specific to the liability. When the discount is recognized, the effect of the provision derived from the lapse of time is accounted for as &#8220;Interest expense&#8221; in the statement of income. Based on the analysis carried out, the Bank recognized as provision the amount of the best estimate of the cash flow required to settle the present obligation at the end of each fiscal year. </div></div></div> <div style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 13%;text-indent: 0px;"><div style="display:inline;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">The provisions accounted for by the Bank are reviewed at the end of each reporting period or fiscal year, as applicable, and adjusted to reflect the current best available estimate. </div></div></div> <div style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 13%;text-indent: 0px;"><div style="display:inline;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">In addition, provisions are recognized with specific allocation to be used only for the cash flow for which they were originally recognized. </div></div></div> <div style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 13%;text-indent: 0px;"><div style="display:inline;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">In the event: a) the obligation is possible; or b) it is not probable that an outflow of resources will be required for the Bank to settle the obligation; or c) the amount of the obligation cannot be estimated reliably, the contingent liability shall not be recognized and shall be disclosed in notes. Nevertheless, when the possibility of an outflow of resources is remote, no disclosures shall be made. </div></div></div> </ix:nonNumeric> <div style="font-size: 6pt; margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px;">&#160;</div> <ix:nonNumeric name="ifrs-full:DescriptionOfAccountingPolicyForFeeAndCommissionIncomeAndExpenseExplanatory" contextRef="P01_01_2024To12_31_2024" escape="true" continuedAt="TextSelection_139095913" id="ixv-58206">

This is typically on completion of the underlying transaction or service or, for fees or components of fees that are linked to a certain performance, after fulfilling the corresponding performance criteria. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:26%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Bank typically has a single performance obligation with respect to these services, which is to successfully complete the transaction specified in the contract. </div> <div style="font-size: 6pt; margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px;">&#160;</div>

<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; text-align: left; line-height: normal;"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Service commissions where performance obligations are satisfied over certain period of time</div> </div> </td> </tr> </table> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:26%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Performance obligations satisfied over time are where the customer simultaneously receives and consumes the benefits provided by the Bank&#8217;s performance as the Bank performs. </div> <div style="font-size: 6pt; margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px;">&#160;</div>

<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; text-align: left; line-height: normal;"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Customer loyalty program</div> </div> </td> </tr> </table> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The loyalty program offered by the Bank consists in accumulating points generated by purchases made with the credit cards, which can be exchanged by any reward (including, among other offers, products, benefits and awards) available in the program platform. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Bank concluded that the rewards to be granted originate a separate performance obligation. <td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; text-align: left; line-height: normal;">Deferred income tax: it is assessed based on the separate Financial Statements of the Bank and of each of its subsidiaries and reflects the effects of temporary differences between the carrying amount of an asset or liability in the statement of financial position and its tax base. Assets and liabilities are measured using the tax rate that is expected to be applied to taxable income in the years in which these differences are expected to be settled or recovered. The measurement of deferred tax liabilities and deferred tax assets reflects the tax consequences that will follow from the manner in which the Bank and its subsidiaries expect, at the end of the reporting period, to recover or settle the carrying amount of their assets and liabilities. Deferred tax assets and liabilities are measured by their nominal figures, without discount, the tax rates that are expected to be applied in the fiscal year in which the asset shall be realized or the liability shall be settled. Deferred tax assets are recognized when it is probable that taxable profit will be available against which the deductible temporary difference can be applied. </div> </td> </tr> </table> </ix:continuation> <div style="font-size: 6pt; margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px;">&#160;</div> <ix:nonNumeric name="ifrs-full:DescriptionOfAccountingPolicyForEarningsPerShareExplanatory" contextRef="P01_01_2024To12_31_2024" escape="true" id="ixv-58371">

<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; text-align: left; line-height: normal;"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Fiduciary activities and investment management</div> </div> </td> </tr> </table> <div style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 13%;text-indent: 0px;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">The Bank offers custody, administration, investment management and advisory services to third parties that originate the holding or placement of assets in the name of such third parties. These assets and income on them are not included in these consolidated Financial Statements, since they are not owned by the Bank. The commissions derived from these activities are accounted for as &#8220;Commissions income&#8221; in the consolidated Statement of income. See also Notes 45, 46 and 49. </div></div></div> </ix:nonNumeric> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Accounting judgments, estimates and assumptions</div></div></div> </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The preparation of these consolidated Financial Statements requires the Bank&#8217;s Management to consider significant accounting judgments, estimates and assumptions that impact on the reported assets and liabilities, income and expenses, as well as the determination and disclosure of contingent assets and liabilities, as of the end of the fiscal year. The Bank&#8217;s reported amounts are based on the best estimate regarding the probability of occurrence of different future events. Therefore, the uncertainties associated with the estimates and assumptions adopted may drive in the future to final amounts that may differ from those estimates and may require significant adjustments to the reported amounts of the affected assets and liabilities. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">In certain cases, the Financial Statements prepared in accordance with the IFRS Accounting Standards as issued by the IASB, require that the assets and liabilities to be recognized and/or presented at their fair value. The fair value is the amount at which an asset can be exchanged, or at which a liability can be settled, in mutual independent terms and conditions between participants of the principal market (or most advantageous market) duly informed and willing to transact in an orderly and current transaction. When prices in active markets are available, the Bank has used them as basis for valuation. When prices in active markets are not available, the Bank estimates those values as values based on the best available information, including the use of models and other assessment techniques (for additional information regarding fair value estimates see Note 13). This kind of estimates also applies to the measurement of acquired identifiable assets and liabilities assumed as a consequence of business combinations (see Note 14). </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">In estimating accrued taxes, the Bank assesses the relative risks of the appropriate tax treatment considering judicial and regulatory guidance in the context of the tax position. Because of the complexity of tax laws and regulations, interpretation can be difficult and subject to legal judgment. It is possible that others, given the same information, may reach different reasonable conclusions regarding the estimated amounts of accrued taxes (for additional information regarding income tax see Note 29). </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">In the normal course of business, the Bank is a party to lawsuits of various types. In Note 50, contingent liabilities are disclosed with respect to existing or potential claims, lawsuits and other legal proceedings, and is booked an accrual for litigation when it is probable that future costs will be incurred and these costs can be reasonably estimated. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The measurement of impairment losses under IFRS 9 across all categories of financial instruments requires judgment, in particular, the estimation of the amount and timing of future cash flows and collateral values when determining impairment losses and the assessment of a significant increase in credit risk. These estimates are driven by a number of factors, changes that can result in different levels of allowances (for additional information regarding impairment losses under IFRS 9, see Notes 3.2.4 and 52.1.1). </div> <div style="margin-top: 0px; margin-top: 1.67em; margin-bottom: 1.67em;font-weight: bold;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div></div> </ix:exclude></ix:continuation> <div style="text-align:center"> <div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_139095919_100" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_139095919_101"><ix:exclude> <div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; text-align: center;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">BANCO MACRO SA AND ITS SUBSIDIARIES </div></div> <div style="margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px; font-size: 8pt;">&#160;</div> </ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_139095919_101" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_139095919_102"><ix:nonNumeric name="bma:DescriptionOfAccountingPolicyForStandardsAmendmentsAdoptedInTheFiscalYearPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="P01_01_2024To12_31_2024" escape="true" id="ixv-58427"> <div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Standards amendments adopted in the fiscal year</div></div></div> </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">For the fiscal year beginning on January&#160;1, 2024, the following amendments to IFRS Accounting Standards as issued by the IASB are effective: </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Amendments to IFRS 16 &#8220;Leases&#8221; &#8211; Sale and leaseback transactions</div>: </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">In September 2022, the IASB issued amendments to IFRS 16, specifically on the requirements that a lessee-seller uses in measuring the lease liability arising in a sale and leaseback transaction, to ensure the lessee-seller does not recognize any amount of the gain or loss that relates to the right of use. Applying these requirements will not prevent the seller-lessee from recognizing, in profit or loss, any gain or loss related to the partial or full termination of a lease. The amendment does not prescribe specific measurement requirements for lease liabilities arising from a leaseback. The initial measurement of the lease liability arising from a leaseback may result in a seller-lessee determining &#8216;lease payments&#8217; that are different from the general definition of lease payments. The seller-lessee will need to develop and apply an accounting policy that results in information that is relevant and reliable in accordance with IAS 8. </div> <div style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 7%;text-indent: 0px;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">This amendment did not have a material impact on the consolidated Financial Statements. </div></div></div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Amendments to IAS 7 &#8220;Statement of Cash Flows&#8221; and IFRS 7 &#8220;Financial Instruments: Disclosures&#8221; &#8211; Disclosures on supplier finance arrangements</div>: </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">In May 2023, the IASB issued amendments to IAS 7 &#8220;Statement of Cash Flows&#8221; and IFRS 7 &#8220;Financial Instruments: Disclosures&#8221;, which specify disclosure requirements to enhance the current requirements, which are intended to assist users of financial statements in understanding the effects of supplier finance arrangements on an entity&#8217;s liabilities, cash flows and exposure to liquidity risk. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">These amendments require an entity to provide information about the impact of supplier finance arrangements on liabilities and cash flows, including terms and conditions of those arrangements, quantitative information on liabilities related to those arrangements as at the beginning and end of the reporting period and the type and effect of non-cash changes in the carrying amounts of those arrangements. The information on those arrangements is required to be aggregated unless the individual arrangements have dissimilar or unique terms and conditions. In the context of quantitative liquidity risk disclosures required by IFRS 7, supplier finance arrangements are included as an example of other factors that might be relevant to disclose. </div> <div style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 7%;text-indent: 0px;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">These amendments did not have material impacts on the disclosures of the consolidated Financial Statements. </div></div></div> </ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric name="bma:DescriptionOfAccountingPolicyForNewAccountingPronouncementsExplanatory" contextRef="P01_01_2024To12_31_2024" escape="true" continuedAt="TextSelection_139095918" id="ixv-58446"> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">New pronouncements</div></div></div> </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The new and amended standards and interpretations that are issued, but not yet effective, up to the date of issuance of these consolidated Financial Statements are disclosed below. The Bank intends to adopt these standards, if applicable, when they become effective. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Amendments to IAS 21 &#8211; Lack of exchangeability</div> </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">In August 2023, the IASB issued amendments to IAS 21 related to &#8220;Lack of exchangeability&#8221;. The amendment to IAS 21 specifies how an entity should assess whether a currency is exchangeable and how it should determine a spot exchange rate when exchangeability is lacking. A currency is considered to be exchangeable into another currency when an entity is able to obtain the other currency within a time frame that allows for a normal administrative delay and through a market or exchange mechanism in which an exchange transaction would create enforceable rights and obligations. If a currency is not exchangeable into another currency, an entity is required to estimate the spot exchange rate at the measurement date. An entity&#8217;s objective in estimating the spot exchange rate is to reflect the rate at which an orderly exchange transaction would take place at the measurement date between market participants under prevailing economic conditions. The amendments note that an entity can use an observable exchange rate without adjustment or another estimation technique. </div> <div style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 7%;text-indent: 0px;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">When an entity estimates a spot exchange rate because a currency is not exchangeable into another currency, it will disclose information that enables users of the financial statements to understand how the currency not being exchangeable into another currency affects, or is expected to affect, the entity&#8217;s financial performance, financial position and cash flows. These amendments are effective as of January&#160;1, 2025. The Bank is evaluating the effects that this amendment would cause on the consolidated Financial Statements. </div></div></div> <div style="margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px; font-size: 8pt;">&#160;</div> <div style="margin-top:0pt; The Bank is also exposed to overdrafts and unused agreed credits on credit cards of the Bank. margin-bottom: 0px; font-size: 8pt;">&#160;</div> <ix:nonNumeric name="ifrs-full:DisclosureOfDerivativeFinancialInstrumentsExplanatory" contextRef="P01_01_2024To12_31_2024" escape="true" continuedAt="TextSelection_139095868" id="ixv-59903">

<td id="fin865064_12" style="width:7%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">6.</div></div></td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; text-align: left; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">DERIVATIVE FINANCIAL INSTRUMENTS </div></div> </td> </tr> </table> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Bank performs derivative transactions for trading purposes through Futures and Forwards. These are contractual agreements to buy or sell a specific financial instrument at a given price and a fixed date in the future. Forward contracts are customized contracts traded on an over-the-counter market. Future contracts, in turn, correspond to transactions for standardized amounts, executed in a regulated market and, generally, subject to daily cash margin requirements. The main differences in risks associated with these types of contracts are the credit risk and the liquidity risk. In forward contracts there is counterparty risk since the Bank has credit exposure to counterparties of the agreements. The credit risk related to futures contracts is deemed very low because daily cash margin requirements help guarantee these contracts are always fulfilled. In addition, forward contracts are generally settled in gross terms and, therefore, they are deemed to have a higher settlement risk than future contracts that, unless they are chosen to be performed by delivery, are settled on a net basis. Both types of contracts expose the Bank to market risk. See in addition Notes 5 and 10. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">At the beginning, derivatives often imply only a mutual exchange of promises with little or no investment. Nevertheless, these instruments frequently imply high levels of leverage and are quite volatile. A relatively small movement in the value of the underlying asset could have a significant impact in profit or loss. Furthermore, over-the-counter derivatives may expose the Bank to risks related to the absence of an exchange market in which to close an open position. The Bank&#8217;s exposure for derivative contracts is monitored on a regular basis as part of its general risk management framework. Information on the Bank&#8217;s credit risk management objectives and policies is included in Note 52. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Notional values indicate the amount of the underlying pending transactions at year end and are not indicative of either the market risk or the credit risk. The fair value of the derivative financial instruments recognized as assets or liabilities in the consolidated statement of financial position is presented as follows. Changes in fair values were accounted for in profit or loss, the breakdown of which is disclosed in Note 34. </div> <div style="font-size: 12pt; margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px;">&#160;</div> <ix:nonNumeric name="bma:DisclosureOfNotionalAndFairValueAmountsOfDerivativeFinancialInstrumentsTableTextBlock" contextRef="P01_01_2024To12_31_2024" escape="true" id="ixv-59916">

<td style="width:7%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left">(1)</td>

In this operation, the options can be exercised up to one day before the expiration of the underlying asset. Considering the terms and conditions of these put options established by the BCRA, they are considered &#8220;out of the money&#8221; with a fair value equal to zero. </div> </td> </tr> </table> <div style="font-size: 12pt; margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px;">&#160;</div>

margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation> <ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_139095868_1" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_139095868_2"><ix:exclude><hr style="color:#999999;height:3px;width:100%;clear:both"/></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_139095868_2" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_139095868_3"><ix:exclude> <div style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 1.67em; margin-bottom: 1.67em;font-weight: bold;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div></div> </ix:exclude></ix:continuation></div> </div> </div> <div> <div> <div style="line-height:normal;display: inline;"> <div style="text-align:center"> <div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_139095868_3" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_139095868_4"><ix:exclude> <div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; text-align: center;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">BANCO MACRO SA AND ITS SUBSIDIARIES </div></div> <div style="margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px; font-size: 8pt;">&#160;</div> </ix:exclude></ix:continuation> <ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_139095868_4"><div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Derivatives held for trading are generally related to products offered by the Bank to its customers. The Bank shall also take positions expecting to benefit from favorable changes in prices, rates or indexes, i.e. take advantage of the high level of leverage of these contracts to obtain yields, assuming at the same time high market risk. Additionally, they may be held for arbitrage, i.e. to obtain a benefit free of risk for the combination of a derivative product and a portfolio of financial assets, trying to benefit from anomalous situations in the prices of assets in the markets. </div> </ix:continuation> <div style="font-size: 18pt; margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px;">&#160;</div> <ix:nonNumeric name="ifrs-full:DisclosureOfRepurchaseAndReverseRepurchaseAgreementsExplanatory" contextRef="P01_01_2024To12_31_2024" escape="true" id="ixv-60413">
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="text-align:start; BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;border:0;width:100%">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td id="fin865064_13" style="width:7%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">7.</div></div></td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; text-align: left; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">REPURCHASE AGREEMENTS </div></div> </td> </tr> </table> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Securities sold under agreements to repurchase at a specified future date are not derecognized from the statement of financial position as the Bank retains substantially all of the risks and rewards of ownership. The corresponding cash received is recognized in the consolidated statement of financial position as an asset with a corresponding obligation to return it, including accrued interest as a liability within cash collateral on securities lent and repurchase agreements, reflecting the transaction&#8217;s economic substance as a loan to the Bank. The difference between the sale and repurchase prices is treated as interest expense and is accrued over the life of agreement using the effective interest method. When the counterparty has the right to sell or re-pledge the securities, the Bank reclassifies those securities in its statement of financial position to &#8220;Financial Assets delivered as guarantee&#8221;. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Conversely, securities purchased under agreements to resell at a specified future date are not recognized in the statement of financial position. The consideration paid, including accrued interest, is recorded in the statement of financial position, within cash collateral on securities borrowed and reverse repurchase agreements, reflecting the transaction&#8217;s economic substance as a loan by the Bank. The difference between the purchase and resale prices is recorded in net interest income and is accrued over the life of the agreement using the effective interest method. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">If securities purchased under an agreement to resell are subsequently sold to third parties, the obligation to return the securities is recorded in &#8220;Liabilities at fair value through profit or loss&#8221;. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">As of December&#160;31, 2024 and 2023, the Bank has repurchase agreements of government and private securities, in absolute value, for <ix:nonFraction name="bma:TransactionCostForReverseRepurchasesOfSecurities" contextRef="PAsOn12_31_2024_GovernmentSecuritiesMemberifrsfullClassesOfFinancialInstrumentsAxis" unitRef="Unit_ARS" decimals="-3" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-128005">18,956,694</ix:nonFraction> and <ix:nonFraction name="bma:TransactionCostForReverseRepurchasesOfSecurities" contextRef="PAsOn12_31_2023_GovernmentSecuritiesMemberifrsfullClassesOfFinancialInstrumentsAxis" unitRef="Unit_ARS" decimals="-3" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-128006">1,391,909,634</ix:nonFraction>, respectively. Maturity of the repurchase agreements as of December 2024 will occur during the month of January 2025. Furthermore, the securities received guarantee repurchase agreements as of December&#160;31, 2023 amount to <ix:nonFraction name="bma:FinancialAssetsOffBalanceSheet" contextRef="PAsOn12_31_2023" unitRef="Unit_ARS" decimals="-3" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-128007">1,479,609,206</ix:nonFraction> and are recognized as an off balance sheet transaction, while the securities delivered that guarantee repurchase agreements as of December&#160;31, 2024 and 2023 amount to <ix:nonFraction name="ifrs-full:RepurchaseAgreementsAndCashCollateralOnSecuritiesLent" contextRef="PAsOn12_31_2024" unitRef="Unit_ARS" decimals="-3" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-128008">23,026,682</ix:nonFraction> and <ix:nonFraction name="ifrs-full:RepurchaseAgreementsAndCashCollateralOnSecuritiesLent" contextRef="PAsOn12_31_2023" unitRef="Unit_ARS" decimals="-3" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-128009">66,301,893</ix:nonFraction>, respectively, and are recorded as &#8220;Financial assets delivered in guarantee&#8221; of the <div style="display:inline;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;text-indent: 0px;display:inline;">consolidated Financial Statements.</div></div></div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Profit generated by the Bank as a result of its repurchase agreements arranged during the fiscal years ended on December&#160;31, 2024, 2023 and 2022, total <ix:nonFraction name="bma:ProfitGeneratedByTheBankThroughRepurchaseTransactions" contextRef="P01_01_2024To12_31_2024" unitRef="Unit_ARS" decimals="-3" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-128010">297,684,162</ix:nonFraction>, <ix:nonFraction name="bma:ProfitGeneratedByTheBankThroughRepurchaseTransactions" contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_31_2023" unitRef="Unit_ARS" decimals="-3" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-128011">428,816,754</ix:nonFraction> and <ix:nonFraction name="bma:ProfitGeneratedByTheBankThroughRepurchaseTransactions" contextRef="P01_01_2022To12_31_2022" unitRef="Unit_ARS" decimals="-3" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-128012">90,088,754</ix:nonFraction>, respectively, and were accounted for in &#8220;Interest income&#8221; in the statement of income. In addition, losses generated by the Bank as a result of its repurchase agreements arranged during the fiscal years ended on December&#160;31, 2024, 2023 and 2022 total <ix:nonFraction name="bma:LossesGeneratedByTheBankThroughReverseRepurchaseTransactions" contextRef="P01_01_2024To12_31_2024" unitRef="Unit_ARS" decimals="-3" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-128013">8,268,119</ix:nonFraction>, <ix:nonFraction name="bma:LossesGeneratedByTheBankThroughReverseRepurchaseTransactions" contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_31_2023" unitRef="Unit_ARS" decimals="-3" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-128014">30,211,753</ix:nonFraction> and <ix:nonFraction name="bma:LossesGeneratedByTheBankThroughReverseRepurchaseTransactions" contextRef="P01_01_2022To12_31_2022" unitRef="Unit_ARS" decimals="-3" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-128015">6,616,153</ix:nonFraction>, respectively, and are recognized as &#8220;Interest expense&#8221; in the Statement of income. </div> </ix:nonNumeric> <div style="font-size: 18pt; margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px;">&#160;</div> <ix:nonNumeric name="bma:DisclosureOfOtherFinancialAssetsExplanatoryTextBlock" contextRef="P01_01_2024To12_31_2024" escape="true" id="ixv-60430">

<td id="fin865064_15" style="width:7%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">9.</div></div></td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; text-align: left; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">LOSS ALLOWANCE FOR EXPECTED CREDIT LOSSES ON CREDIT EXPOSURES NOT MEASURED AT FAIR VALUE THROUGH PROFIT OR LOSS </div></div> </td> </tr> </table> <div style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 7%;text-indent: 0px;"><div style="display:inline;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">The Bank recognizes a loss allowance for expected credit losses on all credit exposures not measured at fair value through profit or loss, like debt instruments measured at amortized cost, debt instruments measured at fair value through other comprehensive income, loan commitments and financial guarantee contracts (not measured at fair value through profit or loss), contract assets and lease receivables. </div></div></div> <div style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 7%;text-indent: 0px;"><div style="display:inline;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Note 13 discloses financial assets measured at fair value on a recurring basis and financial assets not recognized at fair value. This classification is made pursuant to the expressed in Note 3 &#8220;Basis for the preparation of these consolidated Financial Statements and applicable accounting standards&#8221;. Additionally, Note 13 explains the information related to the valuation process. </div></div></div> <div style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 7%;text-indent: 0px;"><div style="display:inline;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Moreover, the Bank applies the impairment requirements for guarantees granted, undrawn commitments of credit cards, checking account advance agreements and letters of credit, which are not recognized in the consolidated statement of financial position. This impairment is disclosed in the consolidated statement of income as &#8220;Other operating expenses&#8221;. </div></div></div> <div style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 7%;text-indent: 0px;"><div style="display:inline;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">For the purpose of assessing the Bank&#8217;s credit risk exposure and identifying material credit risk concentration, disclosures regarding credit risk of financial assets and off balance items are as follows. </div></div></div> <div style="font-size: 6pt; margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px;">&#160;</div> <ix:nonNumeric name="ifrs-full:DisclosureOfCreditRiskExposureExplanatory" contextRef="P01_01_2024To12_31_2024" escape="true" id="ixv-60685">

<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="text-align:start; BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;border:0;width:100%">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td id="fin865064_19" style="width:7%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">13.</div></div></td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; text-align: left; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">FAIR VALUE QUANTITATIVE AND QUALITATIVE DISCLOSURES </div></div> </td> </tr> </table> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The fair value is the amount at which an asset can be exchanged, or at which a liability can be settled, in mutual independent terms and conditions between participants of the principal market (or the most advantageous market) who are duly informed and willing to transact in an orderly and current transaction, at the measurement date under the current market conditions whether the price is directly observable or estimated using a valuation technique under the assumption that the Bank is an ongoing business. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">When a financial instrument is quoted in a liquid and active market, its price in the market in a real transaction provides the most reliable evidence of its fair value. Nevertheless, when there is no quoted price in the market or it cannot be evidence of the fair value of such instrument, in order to determine such fair value, the entities may use the market value of another instrument with similar characteristics, the analysis of discounted cash flows or other applicable techniques, which shall be significantly affected by the assumptions used. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Although the Bank&#8217;s Management has used its best judgment to estimate the fair values of its financial instruments, any technique to perform such estimate implies certain inherent fragility level. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Fair value hierarchy</div> </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Bank uses the following hierarchy to determine and disclose the fair value of financial instruments, according to the valuation technique applied: </div> <div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="text-align:start; BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;border:0;width:100%">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:10%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:2%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left">&#8226;</td>
<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top">&#160;</td>
<td style="text-align: left; vertical-align: top;"> <div style="text-align: left; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; line-height: normal;">Level 1: quoted prices (unadjusted) observable in active markets that the Bank accesses to at the measurement day for identical assets or liabilities. The Bank considers markets as active only if there are sufficient trading activities with respect to the volume and liquidity of the identical assets or liabilities and when there are binding and exercisable price quotes available at the end of each fiscal year. </div> </td> </tr> </table> <div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="text-align:start; BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;border:0;width:100%">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:10%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:2%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left">&#8226;</td>
<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top">&#160;</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; text-align: left; line-height: normal;">Level 2: Valuation techniques for which the data and variables having a significant impact on the determination of the fair value recognized or disclosed are observable for the asset or liability, either directly or indirectly. Such inputs include quoted prices for similar assets or liabilities in active markets, quoted prices for identical instruments in inactive markets and observable inputs other than quoted prices, such as interest rates and yield curves, implied volatilities, and credit spreads. In addition, adjustments to level 2 inputs may be required for the condition or location of the asset or the extent to which it relates to items that are comparable to the valued instrument. However, if such adjustments are based on unobservable inputs that are significant to the entire measurement, the Bank will classify the instruments as Level 3. </div> </td> </tr> </table> <div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="text-align:start; BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;border:0;width:100%">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:10%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:2%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left">&#8226;</td>
<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top">&#160;</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; text-align: left; line-height: normal;">Level 3: Valuation techniques for which the data and variables having a significant impact on the determination of the fair value recognized or disclosed are not based on observable market information. </div> </td> </tr> </table> <div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; margin-top: 1.67em; margin-bottom: 1.67em;font-weight: bold;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div></div> </ix:exclude></ix:continuation> <div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_139095898_10" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_139095898_11"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; text-align: center;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><ix:exclude>BANCO MACRO SA AND ITS SUBSIDIARIES</ix:exclude> </div></div><div style="margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px; font-size: 8pt;">&#160;</div><div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Description of the valuation process</div> </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The fair value of instruments categorized as level 1 was assessed by using quoted prices effective at the end of each fiscal year in active markets for identical assets or liabilities, if representative. Currently, for most of the government and private securities, there are two principal markets in which the Bank operates: BYMA and MAE. Additionally, in the case of derivatives, both MAE and Mercado a T&#233;rmino de Rosario SA (ROFEX) are deemed active markets. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">On the other hand, for certain assets and liabilities that do not have an active market, categorized as level 2, the Bank used valuation techniques that included the use of market transactions performed under mutual independent terms and conditions, between interested and duly informed parties, provided that they are available as well as references to the current fair value of another instrument being substantially similar, or otherwise the analysis of cash flows discounted at rates built from market information of similar instruments. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">In addition, certain assets and liabilities included in this category were valued using price quotes of identical instruments in &#8220;less active markets&#8221;. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Finally, the Bank has categorized as level 3 those assets and liabilities for which there are no identical or similar transactions in the market. To determine the market value of these instruments the Bank used valuation techniques based on own assumptions. For this approach, the Bank mainly used the cash flow discount model. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">As of December&#160;31, 2024 and 2023, the Bank has neither changed the techniques nor the assumptions used to estimate the fair value of the financial instruments. </div><ix:nonNumeric name="bma:DisclosureOfFairValueMeasurementOfFinancialAssetsAndLiabilitiesDisaggregatedByValuationTechniqueExplanatory" contextRef="P01_01_2024To12_31_2024" escape="true" id="ixv-75616"> <div style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 7%;text-indent: 0px;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Below is the reconciliation between the amounts at the beginning and at the end of the fiscal year of the financial assets recognized at fair value categorized as level 3: </div></div></div> <div style="font-size: 12pt; margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px;">&#160;</div>

top: 0px;display:inline;">The fair values of instruments measured at level 3 are determined by the Bank based on valuation techniques derived from the &#8220;income method&#8221;, whose main unobservable data are related to discount rates, and on which a reasonable change in such input data would not generate significant effects on the consolidated Financial Statements taken as a whole. </div></div></div> <div style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 7%;text-indent: 0px;"><div style="display:inline;"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Changes in fair value levels</div> </div></div> <div style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 7%;text-indent: 0px;"><div style="display:inline;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">The Bank monitors the availability of information in the market to <div style="display:inline;">evaluate </div>the classification of financial instruments into the fair value hierarchy as well as the resulting determination of transfers between levels 1, 2 and 3 at each year end. </div></div></div> <div style="letter-spacing: 0px; <td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; text-align: left; line-height: normal;">Macro Agro SAU (formerly known as Comercio Interior SAU) </div></td></tr></table> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">On May&#160;18, 2023, the Bank acquired from Inversora Juramento SA, <ix:nonFraction name="ifrs-full:PercentageOfVotingEquityInterestsAcquired" contextRef="PAsOn05_18_2023_MacroAgroSAUMemberifrsfullBusinessCombinationsAxis" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-129107">100</ix:nonFraction>% of the capital stock and votes of Macro Agro SAU (formerly known as Comercio Interior SAU), a company engaged in the grain brokerage business. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Special Shareholders&#8217; Meeting held on October&#160;6, 2023 deemed it appropriate and approved the change of its corporate name to &#8220;Macro Agro S.A.U.&#8221; and, consequently, subject to the authorization of the Business Associations Regulatory Agency of the Province of Santa Fe (IGPJ, for its acronym in Spanish), proposed the amendment of section 1 of the by-laws. On October&#160;27, 2023, the proceedings were filed with the IGPJ. Additionally, on March&#160;5, 2024, the Bank was notified of the resolution of the IGPJ, which approved the reform of the by-laws with the name of Macro Agro SAU. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Assets acquired and liabilities assumed</div> </div> <ix:nonNumeric name="ifrs-full:DisclosureOfDetailedInformationAboutBusinessCombinationsExplanatory" contextRef="P01_01_2024To12_31_2024_MacroAgroSAUMemberifrsfullBusinessCombinationsAxis" escape="true" id="ixv-77440"> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The fair value of the assets identified and liabilities assumed as of the acquisition date is as follows (figures stated in thousands of pesos in constant currency as of December&#160;31, 2024):</div> <div style="font-size: 12pt; margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px;">&#160;</div>

As it was explained in the previous paragraphs, dividends were used to pay the liability arising from the purchase, which decreased by USD <ix:nonFraction name="bma:DecreaseInConsiderationPayableToAcquiree" contextRef="P09_29_2023To09_29_2023_MacroAgroSAUMemberifrsfullBusinessCombinationsAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="2" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-129131">558,651.70</ix:nonFraction>. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Additionally, on March&#160;12, 2024, Macro Agro SAU (formerly known as Comercio Interior SAU) distributed cash dividends amounting to <ix:nonFraction name="ifrs-full:DividendsReceivedClassifiedAsInvestingActivities" contextRef="P03_12_2024To03_12_2024_MacroAgroSAUMemberifrsfullBusinessCombinationsAxis" unitRef="Unit_ARS" decimals="-3" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-129132">450,669</ix:nonFraction> (not restated). font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent: 0px;">On December&#160;29, 2022 Banco BMA SAU filed with the former AFIP a reimbursement action under the terms established by the first paragraph of section 81, Law No.&#160;11683 requesting the reimbursement of <ix:nonFraction name="ifrs-full:IncomeTaxesPaidRefund" contextRef="P12_29_2022To12_29_2022_BancoBmaSauMemberdeiLegalEntityAxis_FiscalYearTwoThousandNineteenToTwoThousandTwentyMemberBMATaxPeriodsAxis" unitRef="Unit_ARS" decimals="-3" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-130413">639,325</ix:nonFraction> (not restated) and <ix:nonFraction name="ifrs-full:IncomeTaxesPaidRefundClassifiedAsOperatingActivities" contextRef="P12_29_2022To12_29_2022_BancoBmaSauMemberdeiLegalEntityAxis_FiscalYearTwoThousandNineteenToTwoThousandTwentyMemberBMATaxPeriodsAxis" unitRef="Unit_ARS" decimals="-3" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-130414">965,670</ix:nonFraction> (not restated) paid to tax authorities as income tax during 2019 and 2020 tax periods, respectively, as a result of settling the tax by partially incorporating the inflation adjustment set forth by the Section VI of the income tax Law (according to Decree 824/2019), one sixth (1/6)&#160;in accordance with section 194 incorporated by Law 27541 and computing the updated amortizations only for the fix assets and intangibles acquired since January&#160;1, 2018, plus the related compensatory interest. In the absence of a resolution by the tax authorities with respect to the abovementioned claim, on June&#160;5, 2023 Banco BMA SAU filed an appeal for delay with the Federal Administrative Tax Court (EX-2023- 63876605- -APN-SGAI#TFN &#8211; in process in Courtroom &#8220;B&#8221;, Office 6). On September&#160;15, 2023, the tax authorities responded to the appeal for delay and ordered the accumulation of the file with that of 2017 (File No.&#160;49836-I). </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent: 0px;">Regarding to the tax periods mentioned in the previous paragraph, on May&#160;19, 2023, the former AFIP notified the beginning of an income tax audit, which is in progress. </div> </ix:continuation> <div style="margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px; font-size: 8pt;text-indent: 0px;">&#160;</div> <div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:center;text-indent: 0px;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">F-</div>7<div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">5</div></div> </div></div> <div style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"></div> <hr style="color:#999999;height:3px;width:100%;clear:both"/> <div style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 1.67em; margin-bottom: 1.67em;font-weight: bold;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div></div> </div></div></div> <div> <div> <div style="line-height:normal;display: inline;"> <div style="text-align:center"> <div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto"> <div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; text-align: center;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">BANCO MACRO SA AND ITS SUBSIDIARIES </div></div> <div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</div> <ix:nonNumeric name="ifrs-full:DisclosureOfInterestIncomeExplanatory" contextRef="P01_01_2024To12_31_2024" escape="true" id="ixv-94237">

<td id="fin865064_46" style="width:7%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">40.</div></div></td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; text-align: left; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">ADDITIONAL DISCLOSURES IN THE STATEMENT OF CASH FLOWS </div></div></td></tr></table><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Statement of Cash Flows presents the changes in cash and cash equivalents derived from operating activities, investing activities and financing activities during the fiscal year. For the preparation of the statement of cash flows the Bank adopted the indirect method for Operating Activities and the direct method for Investment Activities and Financing Activities. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Bank considers as &#8220;Cash and cash equivalents&#8221; the item Cash and deposits in banks and those financial assets that are readily convertible to known amounts of cash and which are subject to an insignificant risk of changes in value. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">For the preparation of the Statement of Cash Flows the Bank considered the following: </div><div style="font-size: 6pt; margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px;">&#160;</div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="text-align:start; border-collapse: collapse; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; border: 0px; width: 100%; border-spacing: 0px;">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:10%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:2%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left">&#8226;</td>
<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top">&#160;</td>

font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Additionally, the Shareholders&#8217; Meeting held on April 4, 2025, decided to distribute an amount of <ix:nonFraction name="ifrs-full:DividendsProposedOrDeclaredBeforeFinancialStatementsAuthorisedForIssueButNotRecognisedAsDistributionToOwners" contextRef="P04_04_2025To04_04_2025_DividendProposedToBeDistributedMemberifrsfullNonadjustingEventsAfterReportingPeriodAxis" unitRef="Unit_ARS" decimals="-3" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-130789">300,000,000</ix:nonFraction> (in constant currency as of December 31, 2024) to pay a cash dividend and/or a dividend in kind, representing <ix:nonFraction name="ifrs-full:DividendsProposedOrDeclaredBeforeFinancialStatementsAuthorisedForIssueButNotRecognisedAsDistributionToOwnersPerShare" contextRef="P04_04_2025To04_04_2025_DividendProposedToBeDistributedMemberifrsfullNonadjustingEventsAfterReportingPeriodAxis" unitRef="Unit_ARS_per_Share" decimals="2" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-130790">469.18</ix:nonFraction> pesos per share, prior BCRA authorization. Pursuant to the provisions of Communique &#8220;A&#8221; 8214 issued on March 13, 2025, earning distribution shall be paid in ten equal, monthly and consecutive installments (starting from June 30, 2025, and no earlier than the second-to-last business day of the following months). The amount of each dividend installments shall be paid in constant currency as of each payment date. See also Note 51. </div></div></div> </ix:continuation> <div style="font-size: 18pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;text-indent: 0px;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-size: 18pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">&#160;</div></div></div> <ix:nonNumeric name="bma:DisclosureOfGuaranteesExplanatory" contextRef="P01_01_2024To12_31_2024" escape="true" id="ixv-98753">

<td id="fin865064_49" style="width:7%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">43.</div></div></td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; text-align: left; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">DEPOSIT GUARANTEE INSURANCE </div></div> </td> </tr> </table> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Law No.&#160;24485 and Decree No.&#160;540/1995 created the Deposit Guarantee Insurance System, which was featured as a limited, compulsory and onerous system, aimed at covering the risks of bank deposits, as subsidiary and supplementary to the deposit privilege and protection system established under the Financial Entities Law. The abovementioned legislation also provided for the incorporation of Sedesa with the exclusive purpose of managing the Deposit Guarantee Fund (DGF). Sedesa was incorporated in August 1995. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Banco Macro SA holds a <ix:nonFraction name="bma:PercentageCapitalInterest" contextRef="P03_14_2025To03_14_2025_BancoMacroSaBizlandSauUnionTransitoriaMemberifrsfullSignificantInvestmentsInSubsidiariesAxis_BCRACommuniqueBMemberBMACapitalManagementAxis" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="6" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-130791">9.6905</ix:nonFraction>% interest in the capital stock of Sedesa according to the percentages disclosed by BCRA Communiqu&#233; &#8220;B&#8221; 12<div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">9</div>55 on March&#160;<div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">1</div>4, 202<div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="display:inline;">5</div></div>. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">According to Communiqu&#233; &#8220;A&#8221; 7985 of the BCRA issued on March&#160;27, 2024, deposits in pesos and foreign currency placed in participating entities in the form of checking accounts, savings accounts, certificates of deposits or other forms of deposit that the BCRA may determine, and which meet the requirements provided for in Presidential Decree No.&#160;540/1995 and other requirements that the regulatory authority may determine from time to time, will be covered up to the amount of <ix:nonFraction name="bma:DepositGuaranteeThroughInsuranceMaximumAmount" contextRef="PAsOn12_31_2024_NotificationByBcraThresholdLimitsOfDepositOfCustomersRaisedMemberifrsfullNonadjustingEventsAfterReportingPeriodAxis" unitRef="Unit_ARS" decimals="-3" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-130792">25,000</ix:nonFraction>. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">On the other hand, the BCRA provided from the exclusion of the guarantee system, among others, of any deposits made by other financial entities, deposits made by persons related to the Bank and securities deposits. </div> </ix:nonNumeric> <div style="font-size: 18pt; margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px;">&#160;</div> <ix:nonNumeric name="bma:DisclosureOfRestrictedAssetsExplanatory" contextRef="P01_01_2024To12_31_2024" escape="true" continuedAt="TextSelection_139096067" id="ixv-98771">

This way, the risk of losses is minimized and access to the security is guaranteed in case of the debtor&#8217;s non-compliance. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Trusts usually act as conduits to collect cash from the debtor&#8217;s flow of operations and send such cash to the Bank for the payment of the debtor&#8217;s loans and thus ensure compliance with the obligations assumed by the trustor and guaranteed through the trust. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Additionally, other guarantee trusts manage specific assets, mainly real property. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Provided there is no non-compliance or delays by the debtor in the obligations assumed with the beneficiary, the trustee shall not execute the guarantee and all excess amounts as to the value of the obligations are reimbursed by the trustee to the debtor. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">As of December&#160;31, 2024 and 2023, considering the latest available accounting information as of the date of issuance of these consolidated Financial Statements, the assets managed by Banco Macro SA and Macro Fiducia SAU, amounted to <ix:nonFraction name="bma:FinancialAssetsManagedByBank" contextRef="PAsOn12_31_2024" unitRef="Unit_ARS" decimals="-3" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-130852">4,732,462</ix:nonFraction> and <ix:nonFraction name="bma:FinancialAssetsManagedByBank" contextRef="PAsOn12_31_2023" unitRef="Unit_ARS" decimals="-3" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-130853">1,746,420</ix:nonFraction>, respectively. </div> <div style="font-size: 6pt; margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px;">&#160;</div>

<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; text-align: left; line-height: normal;">Tax claims </div> </td> </tr> </table> <div style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The former AFIP and tax authorities of the relevant jurisdictions have reviewed the tax returns filed by the Bank related to income tax, minimum presumed income tax and other taxes (mainly turnover tax). As a result, there are claims pending at court and/or administrative levels, either subject to discussion or appeal. The most significant claims are summarized below: </div> <div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>

Moreover, the Bank adheres to the good banking practices included in the Financial Entities Corporate Governance Guidelines, as supplemented of the BCRA. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent: 0px;">The Bank publicly trades its shares on the Buenos Aires Stock Exchange (BCBA, for its acronym in Spanish) and, thus, it is subject to the regulations issued by the CNV. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent: 0px;">Through General Resolution No.&#160;797/19, the CNV established the minimum contents of the Corporate Governance Code, adding notions of good corporate governance to corporate management as guidelines or recommendations that seek to provide transparency thereto. The CNV annually requires the issuance of a report in which financial institutions have to explain how the recommendations are implemented or to explain the reasons why it decided not to adopt the good practices described in such resolution. The Bank annually publishes a document called Corporate Governance Explanatory Report together with the Annual Report to the Shareholders for the fiscal year, required by regulations, which is available on the Bank&#8217;s website and on that of such enforcement agency. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; and &#8220;protection of the stability of financial entities and financial intermediaries&#8221;. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent: 0px;">On the other hand, as the Bank lists its shares on the NYSE, qualifying as a foreign private issuer, it is required to comply with certain corporate governance standards as established in section 303A of the NYSE&#8217;s Listed Company Manual, as amended. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; The trust provided by shareholders, customers and the general public depends to a large extent on compliance with these principles. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Likewise, the Bank has a specific Code of Conduct for stock market practices as a framework that helps unify standards of conduct at Banco Macro SA and the Group&#8217;s subsidiaries, in order to strengthen integrity and transparency in the Bank&#8217;s and its subsidiaries&#8217; stock market operations. </div> <div style="font-size: 6pt; margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px;">&#160;</div>

<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; text-align: left; line-height: normal;">Anticorruption policy </div> </td> </tr> </table> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Pursuant to Law No.&#160;27401 (Law on Corporate Criminal Liability), the Board establishes that officers and employees of the Bank and its subsidiaries shall not offer to pay, pay or authorize the payment of money or anything of value to (public) officers to obtain or keep a business. It also extends these guidelines to the private sphere. These principles are contained in the Code of Ethics for directors and senior managers, and the Code of Conduct for all employees. Besides, the Bank has a Code of Conduct for suppliers. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The laws of other jurisdictions with similar prohibitions apply, especially the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act (FCPA), because Banco Macro SA is a foreign company that lists its shares in the NYSE and is subject to SEC control and oversight. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Group companies that wish to perform any transaction involving any public administration officer, public agency or public company, either Argentine or foreign, shall communicate this event in advance to the Board through the General Manager and inform, before the transaction is conducted, the agents or intermediaries that may be involved in the transaction. The Bank also has a manual with guidelines for interacting with public officers. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">This communication duty is not mandatory for the transactions derived from agreements with provincial financial agents (except for the subscription of framework agreements), ordinary bank transactions (for example, payroll processing) and the transactions that do not pose any major risk due to the minimum amounts involved. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Although these anticorruption policies are aimed at transactions within the public sector, they also apply to transactions between private parties, as specifically set forth in the Code of Ethic and the Code of Conduct. </div> <div style="margin-top: 0px;
